newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steadies as traders fix on arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steadies as traders fix on arbitrage.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were steady on Monday as traders waited for the NYMEX to determine if the U.S. arbitrage would fully open and revitalise the cash market.

"Refineries are basically running full blast to cover the distillates, but they are also producing mogas and it will pile up unless the arb opens again," said one trader in Germany. "To my knowledge it hasn't opened again."
Traders said the arbitrage to the U.S. had reopened on Friday for big cargoes and a 60,000 tonne vessel was heard sold to the U.S. for loading February 10.
Eurograde barges were unchanged at $214/$217 a tonne for fob ARA material, while Feb NYMEX gasoline in overnight ACCESS trading fell 0.19 cent to 67.90 cents a gallon.
A 2,000 tonne Eurograde barge was confirmed sold at $215 for Rotterdam refinery material, and another barge was heard but not confirmed sold at that same level.
Separately, Phillips Petroleum said on Monday it reopened its 100,000 barrel per day refinery on north Tees, England, after it was shut for inspection last week because of a small fire.
"Demand is very relaxed in mogas," in Germany, the trader said.
Gasoline prices appeared unmoved by news of a tanker collision over the weekend in French waters northeast of the British port of Dover.
The tanker Bona Fulmar was carrying 58,447 tonnes of unleaded gasoline from Antwerp for delivery into New York Harbor, when it collided with the chemical tanker Teoatl.
Some 7,000 tonnes of spilled gasoline dispersed.
A spokesman for Oslo-based Bona Shipping, the vessel's managers, said no ships had been delayed or diverted by the accident.
